dossier.architecture: Chassis-aimed non-turret scorer: an initially divided shooter revised to a wider 2.75-width arrangement, belt-floor feed and expanding hopper. Team distinguishes almost 70 nominal capacity from typical 50–60 in play; useful throughput, not nominal storage alone, is the optimization reference.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module specification unresolved here.
subsystems.intake: Rack-driven collector; damaged rack teeth were repaired using sections of spares during championship-level defense.
subsystems.transfer: Belt floor and eight compliant wheels feed an S-shaped path; access panel lifts for electronics service.
subsystems.scoring: Originally separate large shooters jammed; central obstruction removed for one continuous drum. Four shooter motors and adjustable hood.
subsystems.endgame: Front flippy-hook concept conflicted with shooter; side harpoon used with vision alignment, but removed for the filmed event circumstances because net could catch. Team would climb when useful for RP.
subsystems.controls: Second Limelight repurposed for climb after competing pose estimates caused aiming trouble.

versions: Dual shooters changed to continuous drum.
Filmed at state championship before Worlds; reported 65–70 capacity belongs to this configuration.
dossier.analysis: The high-capacity route needs a maintenance plan for racks, a dependable bump crossing and explicit net/climber clearance. The presence of a climb in CAD is different from choosing to install and use it in a particular match. New 1833 design-transfer study: docs/context/1833-reference-2026-7769.md. Historical success does not waive the current no-support/no-turret mandate or certify causal performance.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-7769 · Passive feed solved one jam while rack durability remained unresolved
context_documents.body:
# 2026-7769: Passive feed solved one jam while rack durability remained unresolved

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The rack collector and belt floor feed an originally divided shooter that became one continuous drum. In the team’s later technical discussion, powered upper/lower indexing rollers overpacked the ramp; immobilizing the lower rollers corrected that feed issue. The static hood avoids an exposed powered-roller belt. The team separately reports repeated polycarbonate rack-tooth failures and a 45-A deploying/5-A deployed current-limit strategy at Worlds.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The stated priorities are simple, durable mechanisms and resistance to trench contact. The lower surface was made static to meter entry rather than forcing fuel into a congested ramp. The current-limit change aimed to let the intake collapse under impact; failures became less frequent but did not disappear.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This example needs two distinct failure histories. A feed-path change can be successful while the deployment structure remains unreliable. Stronger propulsion is not automatically the fix for a packing jam, and a high-performing alliance run does not certify rack durability. Source-reported storage also has a useful distinction: almost 70 geometric capacity versus commonly 50–60 in play. Protected interior PETG vector wheels surviving a season is not evidence that the same prints would survive as exposed intake wheels.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test the passive lower feed with full hopper pressure and varied fuel. Instrument deployment impact/current and inspect tooth-root damage. A proposed decoupling of intake sides is a future idea, not a fielded fix.

## Limits

Focused interview plus first-party technical replies 5, 8, 11, 13 and 15 in topic 521008. Tech-slide access returned Gone; the slides were not reviewed or counted as a binder.

context_documents.title: 2026-7769 optimization reference for elite simple architecture
context_documents.body:
## 7769, 2026 CHUNK: flow, durability and honest failure history

Primary facts: the release describes a two-chamber shooter revised to a 2.75-width configuration, almost 70 nominal capacity and typically 50–60 in play. Team replies describe a static hood avoiding an exposed hood belt, and a feed jam corrected by stopping the lower indexing rollers. They also report rack-tooth breakage that persisted despite current-limit mitigation, with spares and repairs needed. Their linked technical slides currently display that the file was deleted. Those slides were not read. The retained mirror snapshot ranks 7769 fourth worldwide at EPA 309.29; it is a dated snapshot, not live verification. Official event results support an elite competitive season.

1833 transfer analysis: the useful principle is that usable match throughput is a system property. More capacity can add loaded inertia, acquisition dwell and feed pressure. More powered contact can make a congested path worse. Begin with a clear hypothesis about the limiting stage, instrument occupancy and delay at each transition, and change one stage before attributing a scoring gain. Test the near-empty, partly full and fully packed states separately. Under a defended shot, distinguish lost aim time, inaccessible geometry, supply starvation and a genuine mechanical jam. A simple hood can reduce interfaces and service work, but its advantages depend on the scoring aperture and collision environment of the new game.

The rack failure is an equally important lesson. Do not label every CHUNK component an optimized design merely because the robot performed exceptionally. Borrow the output discipline and diagnose its failure modes; do not recreate a known weak load path without a correction hypothesis and impact test. Preserve version labels so an early divided shooter and later wider arrangement are not combined into an imaginary single fielded version. The owner's desire to emulate 7769 means elite execution of a coherent primary scorer, not a requirement for a particular hopper size, rack intake or lane count in 2027.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-7769-cad-tech-slides-chunk/521008 (posts 1,5,8); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-7769-cad-tech-slides-chunk/521008/15 ; https://www.thebluealliance.com/team/7769/2026 ; `tables/season_epa.jsonl`; existing `docs/research_continuation/2026-7769.md`. Tech slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/19V4ULNr7_ooZ6yJXtI6NRUoB1uEt86Wnw5UOy8DofH0/edit?usp=sharing — browser reports deleted. Existing interview reference https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU remains source navigation, not a new watch in this pass.
